It is designed to thrive in complex operating scenarios where variability and real-world conditions make traditional, rigid automation obsolete, including high-mix, low-volume production.
High-Mix Production Breaks Traditional Automation
Rigid programming cannot scale when production changes every day.
Acteris reduces the burden of deploying and operating robotic automation, especially within high-mix industrial processes.
Adapt jobs and process variations without rewriting robot programs.
Real-time production monitoring for status, progress, and performance.

Acteris is a robot application software layer that helps integrators and OEMs deploy production-ready robotic cells faster, with less custom code and more repeatability.

Build faster. Deploy consistently. Earn customer trust. Acteris changes the equation by standardizing deployment and execution while preserving the flexibility integrators need to deliver differentiated solutions across industrial and collaborative robots.
Reduce programming burden
Acteris provides reusable robot skills and standardized runtime behavior enabling integrators to deliver high-value automation with less custom code, fewer one-off scripts, and lower maintenance.
Acteris supports new cell deployments and retrofits of existing workcells, providing integrators with a repeatable way to modernize automation and scale across installed fleets without full rebuilds.
Shorten project timelines
Deploy faster with repeatable commissioning workflows, simulation-first validation, and structured rollout tooling reduces integration effort and accelerates time-to-production for end customers.
Acteris includes a production-grade operator workflow for job execution, changeovers, and monitoring, improving adoption on the shop floor while reducing support overhead after deployment.

Acteris is designed to turn one-off robotic projects into repeatable products. Partners can configure, deploy, and extend application behavior while keeping a consistent backbone for execution and operations across customers.
Turn project delivery into a scalable product motion.
Less custom programming per deployment
More predictable commissioning and support

Acteris supports a growing library of production-ready robot skills through a standardized deployment and execution platform. Pick-and-place and machine tending are our first production environments, and the platform is built to expand into additional applications by continuously training, validating, and rolling out new skills while preserving the same platform foundation.

Explore the latest announcements, media coverage, and press releases from Trener Robotics. Stay informed on company milestones, strategic partnerships, and product innovations shaping the future of industrial automation.
Nine integration companies came together in San Jose to explore deploying physical AI and robot skills, exchange customer experience and contribute to Trener’s product roadmap.

Trener builds robot skills and the platform to deploy them on robots. Our partners build the cells, commission them and support customers afterwards. Bringing physical AI onto a production floor depends on that relationship, and on giving integrators the tools and support to deliver it.

“These teams have spent decades making robots work for customers. Their craft, precision and depth of knowledge command enormous respect. Very few companies in the world can deploy robots as well as they can. Trener’s job is to make sure the robots they deploy never get outcompeted in intelligence.

We set out to strengthen partners’ confidence in Acteris and robot skills, give them a voice in what we build next, and connect the Integration Suite with the practical work of delivering customer projects.
Confidence in robot skills on the production floor

Acteris demonstrations across ABB, Universal Robots and FANUC hardware showed the same skill set running across different robot brands. Partners could explore how those skills apply to customer environments and discuss the practical requirements of a deployment.

The Integration Suite sessions focused on helping partners prepare and commission cells more efficiently. Connecting its tools with real integration tasks gave partners a clearer view of how to make the process easier to repeat across customer projects.
Connecting production experience with future capabilities

A visit to a machine shop near San Jose connected the demonstrations with daily production. Partners saw Acteris running parts to a real schedule and spoke with the operators who use it every day. A live session on advanced AI capabilities also showed how a model learns capabilities and how those capabilities are implemented in practice on a robot.

Partners brought experience from customer projects into the product roadmap discussions, sharing and ranking the priorities that matter most to them. Their feedback gives Trener a clearer view of where future capabilities can make a practical difference.
Partners shared their perspectives on what Acteris, the Integration Suite and new robot skills could mean for their businesses, their customers and future automation projects.

“Acteris is a great product, it gives [their] customers the opportunity to troubleshoot and turn over their machines, and it gives customers the confidence to automate almost anything that comes into the shop.”

"With Trener, we receive a huge toolbox of new ways of automating problems that we simply couldn't automate before. Now, with these new capabilities, we are able to do that, and I'm really excited about the new possibilities we will have together."

Partners left with firsthand experience of how Acteris and the Integration Suite support customer projects, how robot skills are learned and deployed, and how their input helps shape Trener’s product roadmap. Across the three days, these sessions connected physical AI capabilities with the integration and deployment work.

We are on a mission to deploy physical AI and robot skills on production floors. Our partner ecosystem is crucial to that mission: integrators turn those capabilities into working cells, support the people who use them and help us understand what manufacturers need next.

The foundational intelligence layer for software-defined robotics: Acteris turns standard robots into intelligent operators that see, learn, and adapt.
Acteris is the Intelligence Layer for Industrial Robots

Powered by Physical AI, Acteris works across leading industrial robots, including collaborative robots (cobots). It is designed to thrive in complex operating scenarios where variability and real-world conditions make traditional, rigid automation obsolete, including high-mix, low-volume production.
Acteris reduces the burden of deploying and operating robotic automation, especially within high-mix industrial processes.

At Trener Robotics, innovation begins with people. Our global team brings together AI and robotics experts alongside industry leaders with deep technical and business knowledge. Together, we are shaping smarter and more accessible automation, transforming industrial operations across applications and driving the next generation of intelligent manufacturing.

From October 19 to 21, 2026, partners from Europe and the United States gathered at Trener’s San Jose headquarters for our first Partner Summit. The focus was on what we can deliver together: robot skills that meet manufacturers’ needs, a clearer path from customer opportunity to deployment, and an ecosystem that helps integrators learn from each other.

A visit to a machine shop near San Jose connected the demonstrations with daily production. Partners saw Acteris running parts to a real schedule and spoke with the operators who use it every day. A live session on advanced AI capabilities also showed how a model learns capabilities and how those capabilities are implemented in practice on a robot.

The compute and physical AI session with Velaura and Sanjay Gupta explored how compute shapes what physical AI can do. The discussion connected increasingly capable robot skill models with the computing infrastructure needed to run them, giving partners a broader perspective on what is needed to bring future capabilities into industrial applications.

We are on a mission to deploy physical AI and robot skills on production floors. Our partner ecosystem is crucial to that mission: integrators turn those capabilities into working cells, support the people who use them and help us understand what manufacturers need next.
We are expanding our partner network across Europe and the United States, bringing together integrators who want to help scale physical AI across more industrial applications.
